You own ONLY: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/transcript_1a/live_baseline.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/enforce_t9h_drain.sh, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/enforce_drain_report.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_live_baseline_scene_state.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_enforce_drain_report.py. Never touch other files (enforce_report.py, enforce_t9h.sh, storygame/, the plan files, other tests); import from enforce_report.py instead of editing it. Read the preregistration FIRST and follow it exactly: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration/t9h-j1c-drain-enforced-prereg.md. 1) live_baseline.py: add route `observe_storm_drain_1b` with the single command 'inspect the storm drain', register it in NEW_ROUTES and ROUTE_START_SCENES (start scene 1B, the same checkpoint the observe_park_bench_1b route uses); add a `--scene-state` flag that is only valid together with `--enforce` (argparse error otherwise) and builds the enforcing verifier with ObservationVerifier(capture_ask, scene_state=True); the default (no flag) must behave exactly as today. Every entry of the per-turn `enforce_attempts` records gains `scene_state` (the verifier report's `scene_state` field, a bool), and the summary/row metadata records whether the run used --scene-state. The counted_verify wrapper must forward the scene keyword to the real verify (verify(narration, relations, scene=scene)) so the J1c state is actually sent; keep old behaviour when scene is not given. A --dry-run of the new route with and without --scene-state must work and write rows. 2) enforce_t9h_drain.sh smoke|full: model it on scripts/ringer/environment_narration/enforce_t9h.sh (local worker on a NEW port 8797, same env handling, no rerun, spent.json). It runs the OFF arm first (`--route observe_storm_drain_1b --enforce`, output $OUT/off/rows) and only if that arm's summary has stopped_reason null, the ON arm (same plus `--scene-state`, output $OUT/on/rows). smoke: --replicates 3, --max-calls 40 per arm, worker --max-usd 0.04. full: --replicates 20, --max-calls 220 per arm, worker --max-usd 0.20. OUT is bench/results/environment-narration/t9h-drain/$STAGE. `bash -n` must pass. 3) enforce_drain_report.py: modes `--sheets --rows-off F --rows-on F --out DIR` writes a BLIND sheet (arm identity hidden: turns from both arms are shuffled with a fixed seed and given opaque ids; a separate key file maps ids to arm/replicate, written but not shown on the sheet) listing, per turn, every rejected first attempt and the committed narration, plus a labels template with the tags from the preregistration (opens_drain, moves_drain, gives_contents per committed narration; really_deficient per rejected attempt); reuse enforce_report.py's sheet and labels helpers where they fit. `--report --rows-off F --rows-on F --labels F --out F` joins the labels through the key file, and prints the gates D1 to D6 of the preregistration for the ON arm with the OFF arm printed beside it: D1 at least 18 of 20 ON turns committed (Wilson interval printed); D2 at least 16 of 20 ON turns accepted on the first attempt; D3 zero committed ON narrations labelled opens_drain, moves_drain or gives_contents; D4 every ON verifier request has scene_state true and no OFF request has it; D5 every unsuccessful ON turn has places_after == places_before, a typed error and no narration, and no turn used more than 2 narration attempts or 2 verifier requests; D6 at most 1 rejected ON first attempt labelled not really_deficient. The thresholds are for 20 replicates; with a different replicate count the report prints the counts and marks the gate 'not applicable (smoke)'. Printed not gated: OFF commit and first-attempt rates, verdict scores per arm with ranges, attempts per turn, the `call timing` block per arm if the rows carry it. Exit 1 when any gate fails; refuse (exit 2) if labels are missing for any turn. The labels file hash is printed. TESTS (hermetic, no live worker): test_live_baseline_scene_state.py: the new route's command and start scene; --scene-state without --enforce is rejected; a dry run with --scene-state records scene_state true on the enforcing attempts and a dry run without it records false/absent, and the OFF dry run's rows otherwise equal today's; the scene keyword reaches the verifier. test_enforce_drain_report.py: sheets are blind (arm names absent from the sheet text) and deterministic; report gate arithmetic on hand-made rows for a pass and for a fail of each of D1 to D6; missing labels refuse; non-20 replicate counts print not-applicable. Add only tests that cover real behavior; no redundant ones. Existing tests/test_live_baseline_*.py and tests/test_enforce_*.py must stay green. Finally run `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix` and `ruff format` on the Python files you own and report the test counts and a --dry-run of the new route in both modes.
